request.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit the FIRST image, our Kalistar painted illustration of adult Kainé from NieR Replicant. Change ONLY her standing pose and the two weapons; retain her recognizable face, silver hair with braid and white Lunar Tear flower, left-arm/left-leg bandages, opaque pale blue weathered battle dress and black trim, Aerie canyon scenery and cool daylight. SECOND reference is an official Square Enix figure used ONLY for the exact TWO SWORD silhouettes, grips, and shoulder/low-hand pose. Do not reproduce its figurine finish, text, background, floating book, or toy anatomy. THIRD image Momo is the mandatory Kalistar painting-style guide: visible broad hand-painted brushstrokes, narrative fantasy, natural face planes, tactile worn fabric/metal, no anime, photorealism, CGI or plastic.
POSE: adult Kainé stands firmly on the same stone ledge, torso almost facing us with a slight three-quarter angle, confident defiant gaze toward offscreen danger, restrained protective anger rather than a fashion expression. Her bandaged LEFT arm is bent, LEFT hand visibly gripping a sword hilt beside her left shoulder; that blade rests behind/above her shoulders, extending sideways behind her head with clear spatial separation from face and hair. Her RIGHT arm hangs naturally at her side, RIGHT hand visibly gripping the second sword hilt; that second blade extends diagonally downwards beside her body, tip just above the stones. Exactly two hands, two swords, each handle continuously connected to its blade, no extra handle or blade, no blade crossing through her head or neck.
WEAPONS: faithfully follow the SECOND reference: a matched pair of long, slightly bowed dark steel saw-backed sabres with many closely spaced pronounced angular serrations on the spine, smooth gently curved cutting edge, broad obliquely cut/angular tips with a small hooked return, long wrapped dark grips and small round guards. Both blades about waist-to-ankle length plus handle, notably longer than in image1, convincing gentle curvature like the real reference, not enormous greatswords, not thin straight katanas, not exaggerated crescents. The shoulder sword and the downward sword are the same weapon design and length, allowing natural perspective.
COMPOSITION: full-body vertical 4:5 artwork, preserve the original art dimensions/proportions, pull camera back slightly enough to include both blade tips and feet with 5 percent edge breathing room. Face, hands and torso readable in the middle 65 percent width; quieter sky around upper blade. Natural anatomy and balanced weight on stone. Keep an adult warrior depiction and opaque practical clothing, no sexual emphasis. Original illustration only: NO card frame, typography, interface, logo, watermark or graphic overlay. Repaint pose coherently as one finished composition, never pasted limbs or a doubled weapon.

review: Assistant inspected full generated artwork: shoulder/low-sword pose, two distinct continuous grips, longer gently curved saw-backed blades, left-side bandages, intact feet and weapon tips, existing Aerie scene and narrative painted style. Native card crop check pending.
